en: This room belongs to Ms. Anna.
This room belongs to Ms. Anna. You can hear voices coming from inside.
This room belongs to a Ms. Mercedes.

You listen at the door.
This room belongs to a Ms. Vivian.

You can hear snoring coming from inside. 

She clearly isn't working.
A man is carefully examining the wall here.
A wave of heat blasts through the opening. Nikolai throws up his hands and shouts a barrier into being in front of him, but his body shudders heavily from the effort.
It might be possible to use Nikolai's Emblem to remove the wall here, but it would take a strong surge of magical energy.
Nikolai gives you a soft smile. He is clearly exhausted and overcome.
Nikolai holds out the emblem and points it towards the wall. It begins to illuminate the area.
Nikolai stands frozen in fear, trying to catch his breath. He looks nearly ready to collapse.
Nikolai steadily makes his way down the road.
Somebody who is proficient with magic may still be able to use the emblem by channeling their energy through it, however.
Still shaken from earlier events, Nikolai hobbles down the road. He apparently forgot to ask for his emblem back.
The chest is outlined with a silver trim, and decorated with strange runes. There are a couple of bottles of liquor stashed inside.
The emblem glows for a moment, but suddenly fades. It seems to be tapped of magical energy after its last use.
The old priest holds out his hand tentatively, and you give him the emblem.
The staircase leads down a long way. Most of it is hidden by the darkness, but you can see two flickering lights illuminating the bottom few steps.
Thin trails of smoke billow off from the candles around the magic circle, as if they had recently been extinguished.
This looks like a comfortable place to take a nap, but now is perhaps not the time.
This might be a comfortable place to sleep, but everything else about this room seems unsettling.
This part of the wall has an unusual shape, and is covered in strange etchngs.
This wall looks similar to the one Nikolai opened. It even has the same kinds of markings etched into it.
Try using Nikolai's Emblem here?
Would you like to head down?
You hold out the emblem and point it towards the wall once more, focusing deeply on the emblem's shape. It begins to radiate with a resplendent light.
You hold out the emblem and point it towards the wall.
You suddenly realize that the temperature inside this room is stiflingly warm.

You take a moment to explain what happened. Nikolai's face gradually becomes wracked with sadness and guilt. He turns away for a moment, his breathing laboured and heavy, but trying his best to maintain his composure.
Amongst the empty bottles on the desk are one or two finished potions.
Do you want to attempt to break the spell?
Shifting the crates aside one by one, the way is soon cleared.
The bag is empty, aside from a cumpled up sheet of paper and a lunchbox.
The chest appears to be unlocked. Would you like to open it?
The door you came through has a one-way locking mechanism and cannot be opened from this side.
The main compartment is stuffed with textbooks, but there is a gold ring inside the front pocket. It might come in useful.
The owner of this satchel is nowhere to be seen. Would you like to peek inside?
The scroll's luminescence fades, and it crumples onto the floor.
The spell inscribed on it looks fairly complex--from a quick read, it seems to be used for generating a solid object at a specific location.
There is a mild energy radiating from this scroll.
There is no response. You look to the desk and see a quill standing upright, scratching swiftly against a sheet of paper.
There is something hidden behind this pile of crates.
You can feel a slight cold breeze around your legs here.
You hear an irritated throat-clearing noise coming from around this chair.
This appears to be an ordinary pillar.
This marble pillar appears to be sitting on top of some kind of mechanism.
With a mighty crash, the pillar topples to the floor and cracks in half. Without its weight, the mechanism springs open.
You heave with all your might, but the pillar barely moves at all. It's heavier than you thought.
"I have never seen someone who dared put words such as these to print."

"This Leviathan is the "Jealous Master of our Fates", it says. He is... a living part of the island, who allows life or death, prosperity or suffering, only at his whim. That's rather bleak, isn't it?"
A slightly deranged-looking man putters around the building. When you catch his attention, he stands up straight and flashes a bright smile.
It's the Sunken Prayer you found in the dank grotto.
Sell your copy of The Sumptuous Garden to the book keeper?
Show The Commanding Oak to the book keeper?
Show the Abstract Print to the book keeper?
Show the Arcane Tome to the book keeper?
Show the Grimoire Halex to the book keeper?
Show the Grimoire Solaris to the book keeper?
Show the Luxicon to the book keeper?
Show the Maxicon to the book keeper?
Show the Nixicon to the book keeper?
Show the Poxicon to the book keeper?
Show the Rexicon to the book keeper?
Show the Salvaged Mantra to the book keeper?
Show the Shadow Psalm to the book keeper?
Show the Sunken Prayer to the book keeper?
Show the Taboo Manifest to the book keeper?
The book keeper browses the pages of the book, his eyes going wide.
The book keeper carefully applies a foul-smelling fluid to a few pages of the book with a soft brush.
The book keeper looks a little nervous, but he swallows hard and meets your eyes.
The book keeper quickly tucks the book into a drawer on his desk and acts nonchalant. He nudges the gold toward you and pretends to be doing something else.
There is a dormant crystal here. Will you try to charge it?
Inside this end table is an amulet, similar to the ones worn by the doctors you have encountered.
There is a key tucked into the top drawer here.

There is a note on this table. It reads, "Make sure that you check the refugees. If any of them got ahold of a key, we could have a break in quarantine, and I don't need to tell you how bad that would be."
This figure makes no motion to attack, and when you approach, the head he holds in his outstretched hand begins to speak.
This sign post is ancient. It reads, "Quarantine Zone".
After a few turns, the water becomes deeper, and the current gentler. You can no longer reach the floor, so you let the water carry you onward.
As quietly as possible, you begin teasing the boards apart, hiding each one underneath the bed as you go.
At their head is a woman, strikingly beautiful but for a severely discoloured front tooth.
Being mindful to check on the guards regularly, you eventually clear a way into the adjacent cell.
Go down the ladder?
It looks as if it could simply be pulled down, with some effort.
Next to the papers is a slightly rusted copper key. You decide to take it with you.
One of the boards snaps in half, and gives you a nasty splinter.
Something hard strikes the side of your head, and your body goes limp.
Soon, you see a faint light coming from up ahead. As you float closer, you see another jetty, jutting out into the flow. You grab hold of it as you float closer and haul yourself out of the drink.

The air coming from below is quite chilly, but feels refreshing.
You can hear the sound of rushing water.
The band of ruffians begin rifling through your pockets.
The chest is empty.
The water is not very deep, but it is very cold, and the tunnel quickly grows dark as the current pushes you away from the torchlit jetty.
The water looks clean, and does not seem particularly deep. You could climb in and let the current carry you downstream, but there is no telling where you might end up.
There is a small stack of papers on the table. You flick through a few shets, but there is nothing that jumps out as being important.
There is a tremendous scuffling, and in an instant, before you can reach for your weapons, you are completely surrounded by scruffy rogues.
There's a small iron key hidden underneath the bed.
This looks like all the gold that was stolen from you.
This section of wall is boarded up.

This tree looks significantly less healthy than the others.
The ground around it is cracked and uneven, and many of its roots are sticking out above ground, as if it had been previously uprooted and put back.
Water flows underneath the jetty at a brisk speed. You notice some pieces of weathered rope tied to some of the posts, suggesting that something is usually moored here.
Whoever worked on this has done a sloppy job. Some of the boards look wobbly and loose. You could probably just smash through, or if you're nimble enough, you might be able to pry them open quietly.

With a mighty shove, the tree topples over to the side,
revealing a hidden door.
With no regard for your own safety, you smash through the wall.
You are numb and shivering, but back on solid ground once more. With any luck, a campfire will be forthcoming.
You decide to step back from the edge. Jumping in seems needlessly risky.
You gently lower yourself off the edge and into the water.
You hear a clicking noise, but nothing happens.
It reads : If not ye guardian be, turn back.
The pedestal is covered with snails and barnacles. There is something written on the very top.
At the bottom, however, you notice a raised, circular section of wood which looks somewhat like a large button. It has the shape of a jewel carved into it.
Climb down the stairway?
Crisp and sweet, with just the right amount of sourness. Truly, you have never tasted a better pickle.
It's delicious! The combination of spices is out of this world. If only there was some warm, honey glazed ham here, too.
It's time to get a move on. You can't just stand around eating pickles all day.
Old, dusty books are scattered across this part of the table.
One of the larger books is inlaid with a green jewel, and looks quite heavy--at least a thousand pages long.
One of the larger books is inlaid with a green jewel, and looks quite heavy--at least a thousand pages long. The shape in which the jewel has been cut looks familiar...
Place the encyclopedia in the chest?
Putting one foot on the first step to make sure it is not an illusion, you carefully begin your descent--one step at a time.
The book is sealed shut, as if the pages have been glued together.
The chest's lid tries to close on your arm! You remove your arm from the chest, and the lid falls back open. There is another click, and the button returns to its original position.
The crystal doesn't react when you touch it.
The encyclopedia fits snugly inside the chest. It starts to sink as its weight pushes down on the button.
The steps near the top are beginning to fade. It would be unwise to try climbing back up.
This cauldron is filled with pickled vegetables. The smell coming off it tempts your tastebuds, but you are unsure how long these have been sitting here.
This plant looks a little withered. You see signs of intentional damage near the base of the pot--there is a small fracture where soil has spilled out.
Which pickle will you try this time?
With some effort, you press down on the wooden disk until it is level with the bottom of the chest. A faint click is heard.
Would you like to read some of it?
Would you like to take the book with you?
Would you like to try one?
Would you like to try pressing it?
You hear a strange, mechanical noise from above.
You slide the book near the table's edge, and carefully heft it into your arms.
You take a closer look, and see a keyring with two keys hidden underneath.
You take one of the pickled cucumbers. The taste is surprisingly sweet and delicate, with a perfect crunch.
Your toes and hands tingle as you look down the stairway. It extends quite a distance, into unfamiliar land.
This appears to be a signal fire meant to be viewed at a great distance.
This corpse has been thoroughly chewed-on by wild animals. There is a small ring among the bones.
This sack seems to be full of foodstuffs. It seems as if this campsite was hastily-abandoned.
Nope.
You find a glimmer of something at the bottom of the... wait, no, that was just the lights playing tricks.
You peer into the chest, looking to find something that was missed by the previous looter. Nothing was found.
You take another look, hoping that this time you'll find something. No such luck.
It reads : Make a offering of perfection to Lord Magister Josiah.
The pedestal is stained brown with ancient blood. There is an inscription on the very top.
After a brief moment, he struggles to stand, his legs shaking under his own weight, and his eyes find yours.
As you approach, the fleshy pod ruptures, and the massive body of a demon topples out, naked and wet.
He looks up once again, his voice more confident this time.
The demon looks down at his own body with amazement, touching his skin with his fingertips as if it is the first time he has seen it.
The naked demon strides past you, still dripping. You watch him climb the ladder, and then he is gone.
There is a journal on the table here.
Will you allow the demon to leave?
As you step through the doorway into the strange yet familiar room, the door locks behind you and a foreboding shiver runs down your spine. It'd be best to not return here.
Etched into the bottom of the empty chest, you can make out the word: "Greed".
From afar, the chapel appears to bright and reverent, but as you approach the entrance, the illusion peels away, revealing the malevolent structure you discovered prior.
The chest is sealed. Is it even a chest at all, or just a stone slab?
A tiny blade slices into your finger. The cut is minor, but it hits you much harder than it ought to. Probably poison.
Sifting through the clutter on the end of the table, you spy a key sitting amid the books.
This chest appears to be locked and protected with a basic trap.
This table is covered with books and various trinkets. You find nothing of particular note.
You spy something glinting on the floor between the pillows. It appears that a key had slipped off the table and been left on the floor.
After having your evening's meal, you lay down in one of them and quickly drift off to sleep.
An unexpected storm has put an abrupt end to your marching, and you've been forced to take shelter.
At least Leftie is happy.
He's obviously quite upset.
In the morning, the sun is bright and the sky is clear. Leftie is in the best mood you have ever seen him in, wide-eyed and eager to get on the road.
In the morning, the sun is bright and the sky is clear. You haven't slept that well in a long time.
In the morning, the sun is bright and the sky is clear. You slept a little too late, but you awoke comfortably tangled in Leftie's arms, and didn't want to wake him.
Leftie crawls under the blanket and into the bed behind you, forcing you to the very edge.
Leftie moves a little, and you feel his beard and his lips brush against the back of your neck, perhaps deliberately, as he whispers near your ear.
Leftie seems in a good mood, and stands a little closer to you than he did yesterday.
Leftie smiles at you appreciatively, and then crawls into the bed, pulling the blankets up around himself.
Leftie, however, looks haggard, and his mood is foul. He'll clearly be needing a long nap when you get back to the stronghold.
You are jolted awake as Leftie's bed gives out from beneath him and dumps him unceremoniously on the floor.
You bar the door and hang your things up to dry. The beds, though old, seem to be in good shape, and after shaking the dust out of the bedclothes, they promise a rare night of comfort.
You barge in and look around nervously, but it seems that nobody is here, and for the time being at least, you're safe and out of the rain.
You have a feeling it's going to be a good day.
You position yourself in front of the door and try to get as comfortable as you can. It looks like you're going to have a long night.
You sleepily settle back against his body, and after a long, indecisive moment, he gently drapes his heavy arm over you and pulls you against him.
You, however, have definitely felt better. Staying up all night in the storm was exhausting. Your back hurts, your feet hurt, and your head hurts too.
It appears that both switches will have to be unlocked before the passage will open.
The Vampire laughs uproarously.
This heavy stone disc appears to be part of the locking mechanism for this passageway. There is a place to insert a key.
The explosion appears to have collapsed part of the cavern wall.
When you open this barrel, there is a sharp click of a device triggering, and the sharp odour of gunpowder. You drop the lid and scramble away from the kegs.

"It's not all bad though, right? I mean, you've got some valuable stuff on you, and now that you're half-dead and I've already seen all your moves, well... I won't even break a sweat. Goodnight, "Champions"."
"What is more important to you personally? Having a strong body, or a being well-known? "
Freshen up before your next fight! Last chance!
The chest appears to be locked, and trying to open it with the Arena Master standing right next to you would be quite rude.
This area is dangerous, and can never be secured.
You gather your party in the arena.
A gentle warmth now fills the cabin. It smells a little like cinnamon!
A large iron key is hidden inside the dresser drawer. Take it with you?
The chest opens with no trouble.
The fireplace has been prepared with kindling and firewood. Would you like to light it?
This canvas bag is ripped to pieces. You notice a couple of objects sticking out from the tattered mess.
This tray is filled with a neat arrangement of cookies. You decide to swipe a few while nobody's looking...
You misjudge the momentum and speed required, and the cookies end up scattered all over the ground. They're fair game now.
You take a box of matches from on top of the nearby crate and ignite the kindling. Before long, you manage to get a good fire going.
A few recently-discarded provisions remain in this sack.
There is nothing inside the chest. It wasn't locked or even properly latched.
This satchel is full of coins, presumably coins the highwaymen stole from other travelers.
Grant wrinkles his nose in disgust.
He turns his head and spits on the floor, then adjusts his crotch, blatantly sizing you up.
There are a few unbroken bottles remaining in this dead man's satchel.
There is a mangled, scraggy tree standing here with barely any branches on it.
This man is dressed in rags. His eyes are sparks of bloody red, and his lips are pulled taut by large fangs. It is very obvious that he is a vampire.
Searching this drawer, you find a long forgotten key in the corner.
There is something still in the quench barrel.
The smell is reminiscent of the fluid you found when you started exploring Zias.
The patch you are standing on appears to be free-floating. You could push off of this sinew to see where it takes you.
There is a cord of nervous tissue stretched tight between  the floor and the ceiling.
There is a cord of nervous tissue stretched tight between the floor and the ceiling.
This sinew is blocking your path to the exit.
Whatever this nerve was controlling should now be released.
You've hit a membrane of some kind. There is no choice but to head back in the direction you came.
In fact, upon closer inspection, it appears that it's not a tentacle at all, but rather some kind of whip-like weapon.
Scything blades cut your hands. You might have better luck if you try again.
There is a vile-smelling liquid filling this basin. You can't see to the bottom, but it looks important.
There is obviously a mechanism attached to the hinge on this chest. Try to open it?
Who knows what could be in there? You leave it alone for now.
Withdrawing your hand quickly, you find that the tentacle isn't actually attached to anything, and comes out of the goo readily.
You disable the blade trap and pop the chest open.
You reach inside, and your hand is promptly grabbed by some kind of tentacle!
A faint smell of hickory lingers in the air here.
The mana battery in your hand tingles as you approach the crystal. You might be able to use it restore the power.
